coverage.row: Baseline: the guest clock is the wall clock and starts at the call's start (green under load)
Baseline: a child that closes the channel then exits is reported by its own exit code, also when the consumer reads the exit only after the grace is due
The consumer owns the deadline: at timeoutMs it resolves timeout; a result sent after the deadline does not win (starved consumer)
F1: a rerun keeps the original deadline; out of budget it is a lost call, not a result (starved consumer)
Declared gap: with a starved consumer, a result sent before the deadline but read after it is timeout
Declared gap: with a starved consumer, a worker lost before the deadline but read after it is timeout, no rerun
Interval create/clear loop next to three neighbours: culprit memory, neighbours exact once
A repeating timer keeps Node's period from the tick's start

findings.summary: Accepted NOTE: the F1 starved case discriminates only when the stall begins before the deadline; on a slow solo spawn a mutant can survive that run; it never false-reds.
